processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) ingots produced by melting raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples aged at 600 °C for 6 h followed by water quenching; this is the aging condition defining the current sample (17Al, 600 °C, 6 h).

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 600 °C for 6 h the α (BCC) matrix of the 17Al alloy has almost completely transformed into β-Mn; numerous fine new BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates are distributed at the β-Mn interfaces.

phases_present.morphology: matrix of near-equiaxed β-Mn grains (Mn-rich phase)
fine precipitates at the β-Mn interfaces
fine particles at the β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: New BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase form at the interfaces between the β-Mn; β-Mn is rich in Mn and poor in Al and Cu, expelling Fe, Al and Cu into the surrounding matrix (Al enrichment favours the BCC phase, limited Cu solubility favours the FCC Cu-rich phase).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average reported

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N, 15 s
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, average reported; electrolytically polished samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the aged 17Al sample (600 °C, 6 h) and track the aging hardening response.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 17Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h: 840.4 ± 18.5 HV (Table 3).

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the phase constitution of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks were found, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn.

characterization_methods.technique: Secondary electron (SE) imaging and EDS analysis (SEM)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging, 50 µm main fields with 2–10 µm insets for the 17Al alloy
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) and new precipitates in the aged alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 17Al alloy the α matrix had nearly fully transformed to β-Mn after aging at 550 °C/6 h; at 600 °C and above the transformation is complete within 1 h and numerous fine precipitates appear inside the β-Mn.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 µm (low magnification) and 0.05 µm (high magnification)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: phase maps and inverse pole figure maps
characterization_methods.purpose: Clarify the microstructural origin of the rapid aging hardening of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels (α→β-Mn transformation and new BCC/FCC precipitates).
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated alloys are single-phase α (BCC); during aging α transforms to β-Mn and new BCC and FCC phases precipitate within the β-Mn.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ion-thinned foils; BF/DF imaging, SAED, HRTEM, EDS mapping
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the microstructures of the ultra-high-hardness alloys, including the FCC Cu-rich phase at the β-Mn interfaces.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fine FCC Cu-rich particles (with FCC twins) form at the β-Mn interfaces; the FCC phase is rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn and slightly poor in Al.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Agilent G200 Nanoindenter; indentation depth 200 nm; test points spaced ≥5 µm apart
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn and the micro-hardness of the hardest aged samples of the three alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h) showed average nanoindentation hardness 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa, with β-Mn intrinsic hardness 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa.

unmapped_findings: EDS-measured chemical composition of the 17Al (Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu at.%) alloy: Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (at.%) (Table 1).

For the 17Al alloy the maximum (peak) Vickers hardness of 924.9 ± 25.8 HV is achieved at 575 °C for 6 h, not at the 600 °C/6 h condition of this sample (840.4 ± 18.5 HV); the optimal aging temperature range for ultra-high hardness in the 17Al alloy was 550–600 °C.

The increase in Al content slowed the β-Mn precipitation kinetics: the α→β-Mn transformation of the 17Al alloy was complete only after 6 h at 550 °C (versus 3 h at 525 °C for 15Al) and within 1 h at 600 °C and above.
